genZNote: Fixes nitrogen without needing a plant host at all — just does it out in the open soil, no symbiosis required.

morphology.shape: Large ovoid rod to coccus, pleomorphic
morphology.size: ~1.5-2 x 2-4 µm (unusually large for a bacterium)
morphology.capsule: Thick capsule; can form dormant cysts
morphology.notes: Protects its oxygen-sensitive nitrogenase enzyme via an unusually high rate of respiration that keeps intracellular oxygen low, rather than by anaerobic sequestration.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Neutral to alkaline soils and freshwater
habitat.hostAssociation: Free-living; not symbiotic and not associated with humans/animals
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Common in agricultural soils; some strains marketed as biofertilizer inoculants

culture.growthCharacteristics: Aerobic; grows on nitrogen-free media by fixing its own atmospheric nitrogen
culture.colonyMorphology: Large, mucoid, often brown-black pigmented colonies from melanin-like pigment

identificationClues: Grows on nitrogen-free media, a defining diagnostic feature demonstrating free-living nitrogen fixation
Unusually large cell size for a bacterium; can form thick-walled dormant cysts resistant to desiccation
Some strains produce dark brown-black melanin-like pigment on aging cultures
Fixes nitrogen aerobically, unlike Rhizobium which relies on a low-oxygen nodule microenvironment

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Growth on nitrogen-free medium (free-living nitrogen fixation)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Fixes atmospheric nitrogen aerobically without a plant host, unlike symbiotic Rhizobium
